text: We rank vendors based on rigorous testing and research, but also take into account your feedback and our commercial agreements with providers. This page contains affiliate links. Advertising Disclosure Website Planet > Web Hosting > Hosting.com Hosting.com (Formerly A2 Hosting) Review: Tested in 2026 Reviewed by: Christine Hoang Written by: Suzanne Stewart Hosting.com is the rebranded A2 Hosting, but does it live up to its former name? Sort of – a lot of the features you may remember from A2 Hosting are present here, and you’ll still get great first-time discounts and premium features. However, high renewal costs and uneven performance may give you pause. First published: July 18, 2025 Number of Updates: 25 Our Score 4.6 Ranked 86 from 3859 Web Hosting Pricing Web Hosting $ 1.99 - $ 8.99 WordPress Hosting $ 2.99 - $ 29.99 VPS Hosting $ 4.99 - $ 60.50 Reseller Hosting $ 22.99 - $ 49.99 Server locations Buffalo ✓ Dallas ✓ Toronto ✓ Mexico City ✓ London ✓ Frankfurt ✓ Mumbai ✓ Sydney ✓ Show more + Check Coupons 3 Visit Site We hosted the same WordPress website on the most popular web hosting platforms and measured their performance Click here to see our results >> Overview hosting.com at a Glance ⏱️ Uptime Guarantee Yes 🔒 Free SSL Yes 🔧 Hosting Types Shared, WordPress, VPS, Reseller Hosting 💡 Basic Plan Features Storage: 30 GB Bandwidth: unlimited Websites: 2 💲 Starting Price $ 1.99 Shared Reseller Dedicated Cloud WordPress hosting.com Pros, Cons, and Things That Could Be Better Shared plans on cloud-based servers Shared plans start at 2 vCPU & 3 GB RAM Pre-installed performance plugins Unlimited bandwidth on all shared plans Custom control panel Only one website per WordPress plan Support team lacks product knowledge High renewal rates I like to compare hosting providers to ice cream flavors. There are those who like to keep things simple with just plain vanilla, chocolate, or strawberry. But then there are others who prefer their ice cream with all the flavors in the world. Triple chocolate fudge cookie, bourbon vanilla bean truffle, and honey salted caramel almond all have their raving fans. Ice cream makers keep inventing new ways to serve up flavorful combinations – and I think the same can be said about hosting providers. They add features, they innovate, they improve. But that really isn’t the case with hosting.com (formerly A2 Hosting). It’s still mostly A2 Hosting — it’s just been rebranded to reflect its sale in January 2025. In fact, I found some old A2 Hosting branding still in place during my tests and marketing features unique to A2 Hosting are still largely kept intact. Hosting.com offers shared hosting, managed and unmanaged hosting for WordPress, cPanel hosting, managed and unmanaged VPS, dedicated servers, and reseller hosting. It’s a good choice for small businesses and individuals , but I can’t recommend it if you’re brand new to hosting. Its proprietary control panel might make it easier to use, but that’s really going to depend on your experience with other dashboards. In the world of ice cream, hosting.com tastes pretty good, but could be phenomenal with some upgraded ingredients. In other words, my testing reveals a few issues with hosting.com that the web host should improve before it joins the ranks of the truly great services out there . 4.7 Features Decent Features That Might Look Familiar If you thought hosting.com would be the new and improved version of A2 Hosting, I have a mixed opinion on this: it nearly is, but there are still some growing pains to work out. In one case, hosting.com missed the mark when it came to one of A2 Hosting’s best features. Custom Control Panel hosting.com’s custom control panel reminds me of the WordPress dashboard Hosting.com claims that its custom control panel is there “to optimize and streamline site management.” It’s supposed to be an option, but according to support and my experience, it’s actually pre-installed. I might be too familiar with cPanel to make an accurate comparison, but I didn’t find it that much easier to use . Mind you, it’s not difficult to use, but it does take some time to get used to the panel. It looks a lot like WordPress’s dashboard, all dressed in black. You have the options menu on the left and your menu selection appears in the main panel. To actually work on your WordPress site, you still have to access your dashboard through your WordPress login. In that respect, hosting.com’s custom control panel isn’t any different from cPanel. There are two things to note about the custom control panel. The first is that it opens in its own browser window. My pop-up blocker was doing its job, so for a moment I thought something was broken. The second is that according to support, it’s possible you’ll lose your WordPress site if you replace the custom control panel with cPanel . Discover More hosting.com Features >> Optimized Plugin Unfortunately, hosting.com’s optimized plugin didn’t work for my site When I first started building WordPress sites, I had no idea how to make them load faster or what settings I could tweak to improve performance without “breaking” something. That’s where hosting.com’s Optimized plugin comes in. It’s an A2 Hosting holdover and one of those features still wearing A2 Hosting branding. The Optimized plugin helps you to fine tune your WordPress settings and then makes suggestions on how you can continue to improve performance. It’s really nice not having to worry about caching, image compression, or forgetting to change the username from the default “admin.” It’s also very helpful that the Optimized plugin keeps the rest of your plugins updated and running smoothly. Unfortunately, I couldn’t get many of the plugin’s features to work . I kept getting an error message that amounted to “You’re not using an A2 Hosting server, so we can’t give you any results.” It wouldn’t give any info on loading speeds, site performance, or stability. Hopefully hosting.com has rectified this error by now. I remember using it with A2 Hosting and it was a nice feature to have. Discover More hosting.com Features >> Performance Plus Surge Protection Performance Plus is hosting.com’s way of saying that it uses servers with load balancing technology to handle high traffic spikes . Hosting.com is using completely cloud-based servers now , and this newer infrastructure helps maintain steady site performance regardless of how many visitors are clamoring at the door. I can see this feature being really useful for sites that run into occasional traffic spikes, such as online stores or blogs running giveaways. Support explained that the feature is available on all its plans , not just for WordPress. So even if you decide to go the shared hosting route, you can take advantage of Performance Plus . Turbo Servers The use of “turbo” language by hosting.com is another A2 Hosting holdover. With A2 Hosting, it simply referred to servers with LiteSpeed and other performance-enhancing technology. Here, I suppose it refers to hosting.com’s cloud-based servers with LiteSpeed . In any case, “turbo” power should dramatically increase your site’s loading speed and performance scores. I’ll get into the details of my performance tests in a bit, but hosting.com did perform decently, so we’ll give these “turbos” a boost. (Bad puns come at no extra cost to the reader.) hosting.com Features at a Glance Free domain name ✔ Free backups ✔ (Managed WordPress plans) Free email ✘ Money-back guarantee 30 days Uptime guarantee 99.9% Data center locations 2 in the US, 1 in Canada, 1 in Mexico, 1 in the UK, 1 in Germany, 1 in India, 1 in Singapore, 1 in Australia 4.7 Ease of use My Hosting Experience With hosting.com There are a few things to watch out for during hosting.com’s signup process, like unclear claims and misleading plan features on its website. But once you complete the signup process, it’s mostly smooth sailing from here on out. Creating a New Account With hosting.com Before I get into the details of becoming a new hosting.com customer, I need to admit that I had some difficulty picking a plan to test. Save for VPS hosting, all plans have the same names. Starter, Plus, Pro, and Max follow you from one hosting type to another. Other issues with hosting.com’s website make it less than transparent, too. There are feature descriptions that are incomplete and/or inaccurate. For instance, despite hosting.com advertising East and West Coast US data centers, WordPress plans only use the Dallas location. And then there’s the content that’s technically true but misleading. This is why I recommend triple checking plan features before signing up. You’ll have to double check the features on hosting.com’s website to make sure they’re accurate The Performance Plus blurb describes it as an option when it’s a standard feature. It also mentions a “Sell plan” that doesn’t exist. And while you can manage more than one site from your control panel via Multisite, each one requires its own separate hosting plan – that’s because WordPress plans limit you to one site per plan . Once I waded through all the confusion the website caused, purchasing my hosting plan was actually fairly simple . If you don’t have a domain name, there’s a handy domain checking tool in the checkout process that searches for your desired domain and suggests other options if it isn’t available. You have to buy a year or more of hosting to get your free domain, by the way. hosting.com’s checkout is pretty straightforward and only involves a few steps You can choose from one of four payment terms: monthly, annually, biennially, and triennially. For WordPress plans, you’ll only have four data center choices. Dallas is the only option available in the US , while London, Frankfurt, and Singapore are your other choices. Payment options are typical: PayPal, credit or debit card, or bank transfer. Connecting a Domain and Installing WordPress WordPress comes preinstalled on all WordPress plans , whether managed or, like mine, unmanaged. That’s one thing that hosting.com got right, as installing WordPress can be a real pain. Not having to do it saved me time and effort – and considerably sped up the setup process. You can easily copy your nameservers, IP address, and other details from hosting.com’s dashboard Another thing hosting.com gets right is making essential information readily available. Your DNS information is one of the first things you see when you open your dashboard for the first time. All I had to do was go to my domain registrar, copy and paste the info required, and wait for the domain to be connected. This took a lot longer than I’ve experienced with other hosting providers by the way, but I have no way of telling if it was hosting.com or my registrar at fault. Once my domain went live, I had my site up and running in a matter of minutes. In fact, it took more time to complete the testing required for our review process than it did to point my nameservers and access WordPress from my control panel. Other Ease of Use Features One-Click Staging Environments I have an uncanny knack for “breaking” websites. If you can stop a plugin from working properly or accidentally mess up one of your theme’s functions, chances are I’ve done it at some point. That’s why I really like hosting.com’s staging and cloning capabilities. On my Plus plan, I had five staging websites available. I didn’t require this feature during testing, but it was nice to know that it was an option. Security Features Hosting.com offers strong security measures for shared plans, such as DDoS protection and brute force defense . These features aren’t always free – some hosts will make you pay for this level of security as a monthly add-on. The pre-installed SSL was another thing that made site setup easier and quicker as I didn’t have to configure anything on my own. Pre-Installed Plugins My site came with 11 plugins already installed , including the (non-functioning) Optimized plugin. Some of the notable ones were the free version of Jetpack, AIOSEO, WP Forms, and Monster Insights. I’m not sure if I’d actually need to use all these plugins, but if you want a no-hassle way to have the most popular and essential plugins for your WordPress site right away or aren’t sure where to start, this can be useful. Speaking of plugins… you’ll only receive automatic data backups with the managed WordPress plans. In addition to this, you can’t manually back up your site from the custom control panel . A workaround is to install a third-party plugin and create localized backups on your computer or cloud storage. 4.5 Performance Good but Uneven Loading Speeds In our previous tests, A2 Hosting had loading speeds ranging from 0.5 seconds to 1.1 seconds and its reliability score was 100%. In my ice cream analogy, A2 Hosting was a pint of Hȁagen-Dazs or an I Caruso gelato. Unfortunately, hosting.com didn’t quite manage to get the same results. Some things to keep in mind before I dive into the analysis – I hosted my WordPress Plus plan on hosting.com’s Dallas, TX data center . And I didn’t integrate Cloudflare CDN, even though I could’ve easily done so through the control panel. Introducing Nutritionism.online, my little test site that could I set up a working WordPress site , complete with a Divi theme, text, and images – this is to make sure we’re realistically testing a functional website. If you’d like to learn more about how we conduct our website tests, check out this article . My hosting.com site’s loading speeds varied from 0.8 seconds to 2.2 seconds. These weren’t as good as A2 Hosting’s previous results, but these speeds aren’t bad for a budget host. On a positive note, my uptime was 100% over the entire testing period. GTmetrix Performance Tests My hosting.com GTmetrix score was good, but not as good as it was with A2 Hosting Since my server was in Dallas, TX, I decided the best option for a monitoring center would be GTmetrix’s Chicago, IL location. My site scored an A overall but the performance and structure scores were lower than what A2 Hosting had registered for the same site (100% for performance, 97% for structure). Because I’ve used the same website for testing, a slow server response would likely explain the drop in score. The spikes in loading speeds for my hosting.com website were worrisome After reviewing the site’s performance during the first week, it looked like the weekend and Monday had the slowest response times. Recent research on online traffic shows that Monday is one of the busiest days for shoppers. If my site had actually been a functioning e-commerce store, think of the traffic I might have lost due to my site slowing down during peak hours . GTmetrix Global Speeds hosting.com scored lower than A2 Hosting in global tests, too When it comes to performance around the world, hosting.com’s results weren’t bad. Loading speeds were great in the US and parts of Europe. Two locations where A2 Hosting struggled were Singapore and Australia – so it’s not surprising that hosting.com can’t manage great speeds here either. It recorded speeds of one full second more for Singapore and 1.5 seconds more for Australia. UptimeRobot hosting.com’s UptimeRobot scores were not disappointing My site’s test results from UptimeRobot were in line with A2 Hosting’s previous results. I had no downtime during more than three weeks of monitoring. This is one area where hosting.com didn’t disappoint. 4.4 Support Support Is Responsive but Not Always Helpful Experience has taught me that support is the one area that’s prone to suffer whenever there’s a big change at a hosting provider. I went in expecting vanilla with sprinkles at best, and that’s pretty much what I got. Hosting.com provides pre-sale support via telephone, live chat, and a knowledge base . Once you become a customer, you can also use a support ticket system. As a “global” host, I wasn’t too thrilled to learn that support is currently only in English. I had a mixed experience with live chat and phone support. The live chat agent was more confused than I was, while the phone agent was more proficient, if a bit slower (as a side note, the phone recording scripts still call hosting.com “A2 Hosting” – this mistake occurred twice during my testing). The hosting.com live chat response time was good, even if the information wasn’t I first contacted live chat to see if I could get some clarification on the Performance Plus feature. The agent was online quickly but didn’t seem to understand my question. After providing a screenshot from the site, I eventually got my explanation I finally posted a screenshot from the hosting.com website and pointed out its features, along with the mention of a “Sell” plan. That’s when the agent informed me that this information was an error and would be rectified. I then tried a telephone call to get advice on backup plugins. The entire call lasted 8 minutes, although I was on hold for 3 of them while the agent reviewed my site setup and looked up the best plugin for me to use. Their suggestion happened to be one of the top-rated free backup plugins. I was pretty pleased with that. They did promise to send an email with further recommendations, but that never materialized. All in all, I’d have to give hosting.com’s support team a decent – but not phenomenal – score. There are other budget hosts out there rocking the whole support thing. hosting.com has a long way to go before it can even come close. 4.6 Pricing Great Upfront Discounts, but Beware the Renewal Fees My site ran on the unmanaged WordPress Plus plan. This plan has more than enough RAM, storage, and bandwidth for the average small business with a decent amount of traffic. But if I were to recommend a package to you, dear reader, I’d go with one of the cheaper shared hosting plans for several reasons . The first is that the plans basically provide the same resources. The entry-level unmanaged WordPress plans offer slightly more RAM than their shared hosting counterparts, but all else pretty much remains equal. The second reason is that shared hosting plans allow more than one website . The last is that cPanel with Softaculous would still provide a straightforward one-click WordPress installation, as well as site backups without the need for an extra plugin. Keep in mind that all shared and WordPress plans come with a 30-day money back guarantee, so if you aren’t a fan of a specific plan, you can back out and get a full refund. If you’re looking for an e-commerce solution, I’d recommend hosting.com’s managed WordPress plans or a VPS hosting plan. The automatic backups offered with managed WordPress plans would be worth the extra fees alone. If you’re new to VPS, hosting.com offers managed plans that are bundled with cPanel. There’s a big upside to hosting.com’s pricing and that’s the incredible initial discounts. The shared hosting plans cost the equivalent of pennies per day (especially if you commit long term), and the unmanaged WordPress plans aren’t far behind. The end of that initial term, however, brings a major surprise. Hosting.com’s price upon renewal can be nearly two to three times the cost of your first term. 1 Compare Our Score 4.9 Compare 1 Compare Our Score 4.9 Compare 1 Compare Our Score 4.6 Compare 1 Compare Our Score 2.4 Compare Hosting.com REVIEW: BOTTOM LINE There are certainly some issues to work out – especially when it comes to support and renewal prices – but hosting.com does boast some nice features for managed WordPress. Its performance isn’t bad either, although I would have liked to see more consistent loading speeds. If you’re looking for a budget host with exceptional performance, helpful support, and affordable long-term prices, Hostinger might be the better option . FAQ Who should consider using hosting.com? Hosting.com is a good fit for small business owners , bloggers, and anyone looking for decent performance without the need for too many advanced features. As a result, it’s probably not a good fit for power users or developers that want specialized tools. Are there hidden fees with hosting.com? While hosting.com is upfront about its base pricing, you should watch out for much higher renewal fees or extra costs for certain add-ons like security features or backups. You may also find you have to buy a more expensive plan to get the features you need. Is hosting.com good for beginners? Hosting.com is generally beginner-friendly , although it’s advisable to check plan details with support before signing up. Once your site is set up, you may need to install extra plugins or tools for tasks like backups, which can feel overwhelming if you’re new to site building. Can hosting.com handle high-traffic websites? Even on its managed WordPress plans, hosting.com won’t be able to handle high-traffic websites. It can handle moderate traffic well, but for very high-traffic or resource-heavy sites, you might want to consider a VPS plan. Alternatively, take a look at our best web hosts in 2026 to see if another service might be a better fit. title: Hosting.com 2026 Review: Fast, Reliable Hosting for Experienced Website Owners - CNET
headings: Value: Decent value for simple websites
The purchase process has some unusual requirements
Website and server management can be frustrating to navigate
Site speed outstripped other hosts’ default speeds
Performance tools are great and automatically enabled
Security: Robust protection from the most common threats
Knowledge base and tutorials are lacking
Hosting.com provides fast, reliable servers and decent value, but it’s only suitable for power users
text: Hosting.com’s fast servers and attractive pricing for shared and WordPress hosting can make it a decent choice for simple websites like professional portfolios and personal blogs. However, setup is overly complicated and customer support is poor, so I only recommend Hosting.com for experienced website owners or folks comfortable learning new tech. To assess Hosting.com, I purchased a plan, built a website, tracked server speed and uptime, tested customer support and analyzed value as well as usability. During my hands-on use, I found Hosting.com a reasonable value web host with exceptional server performance but underwhelming processes that may be off-putting for newcomers. I built a WordPress website with Hosting.com and was disappointed by its unusually complex domain setup process and its lack of site-creation tools. The week I spent tracking my site’s uptime and testing site speed showed excellent server performance, but when I ran into problems, I struggled to resolve them due to poorly trained customer service representatives. Overall, I found Hosting.com’s problems outweighed its benefits, though it may still be a good choice for experienced users building simple websites. More from CNET Getty Image/ Zooey Liao/ CNET Hosting.com 7.4 See at Hosting.com Pros & Cons Excellent server performance Low-cost shared hosting plan perfect for small websites Robust security protocols to protect your website from various types of attacks Overly complicated setup processes Poor customer support Value: Decent value for simple websites Key takeaway: Hosting.com’s rates for shared and WordPress hosting — the best options for most small websites, including personal blogs and professional portfolios — are fairly average. Hosting Type Starting Price Best For Shared $14 per month, $36 for the first year (renews at $168 annually), $67 for the first two years (renews at $336 for the next two years), $90 for the first three years (renews at $504 for the next three years) or $96 for the first four years (renews at $672 for the next four years) Personal websites, for-fun hobby sites, blogs and small business websites not using WordPress WordPress $10 per month, $54 for the first year (renews at $120 annually), $96 for the first two years (renews at $240 for the next two years) or $138 for the first three years (renews at $360 for the next three years) Personal websites, for-fun hobby sites, blogs and small business websites using WordPress Hosting.com’s primary offerings — shared and WordPress hosting — are similarly priced to most traditional web hosts like Hostinger . On paper, this makes Hosting.com a decent choice for budget-conscious users looking to build a for-fun hobby site, blog , professional portfolio or small business website. There’s no specialized e-commerce hosting, and advanced hosting plans like VPS are difficult to navigate, so I recommend an alternative like SiteGround for e-commerce or complex websites. Shared hosting and WordPress hosting Shared and WordPress hosting are low-cost, easy options suitable for small to medium-size websites like blogs, professional portfolios and small business sites. Hosting.com’s Starter shared hosting plan provides above-average value compared to entry-level plans from companies like Hostinger and SiteGround , but higher-tier plans don’t save you much, if anything. WordPress plans have unusually high introductory rates, but long-term pricing is similar to competitors’ WordPress hosting, and the benefits are worth the higher initial cost. Shared and WordPress hosting both use servers with resources (like processing power) split between numerous websites to reduce costs. WordPress hosting generally provides more content management, or CMS, tools, like automated updates. Ease of use: Mildly disappointing Key takeaway: Hosting.com makes purchasing a plan easy, but its website-building and server maintenance processes are unnecessarily difficult to use. Hosting.com’s purchase process seemed promising, but things became progressively more complicated as I tried to build my site. I bought a WordPress hosting plan specifically to test its WordPress hosting tools, and was disappointed by the lack of a setup wizard or onboarding plugin like those offered by SiteGround and Hostinger. Additionally, server management was unintuitive, making Hosting.com a poor choice for beginners. I only recommend Hosting.com if you’re familiar with web hosting or eager to learn. The purchase process has some unusual requirements Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET Hosting.com’s transparent pricing is a breath of fresh air, and the overall purchase process is relatively straightforward, albeit not as streamlined as Hostinger’s one-page checkout. The introductory and renewal prices for the full contract term appear below the per-month rates, preventing sticker shock on checkout. While this seems basic, Hosting.com is the only web host I’ve tested in 2026 with such transparent pricing. The first checkout page for shared hosting displays contract length and domain selection. Upsells for services like domain privacy appear after you choose a domain. None are preselected, but you’ll need to scroll past them and enter your SLD or second-level domain — the name of your website, like CNET in cnet.com — to move forward. This is unusual and may be frustrating for beginners who don’t know what an SLD is. However, the rest of the process is simple, with clear instructions for creating an account and entering billing information. Notably, purchasing a WordPress hosting plan is different, with a separate upsells page before you confirm your contract length. This is annoying, but the upsells aren’t pre-selected, so it’s easy to skip. Once you get past it, the purchase process becomes identical to buying shared hosting. Account management is intuitive Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET Hosting.com’s account dashboard makes it easy to get started with checklists for your products and account. The top menu links to key services like domains and websites. However, this menu confused me at first because it didn’t show any products under the hosting and servers or websites sections, even after I set up my test site. I eventually found my hosting plan in the application hosting area. This placement is unusual, but logical, as WordPress is an application. A left-hand toolbar included links to other key account management areas, including Managed WordPress — where I conducted most of my website-related tasks — and Billing. I appreciated the easily accessible billing settings, as many competitors like Hostinger hide them in dropdown menus. Website and server management can be frustrating to navigate Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET Hosting.com’s website and server management isn’t as user-friendly as most competitors’, performing especially poorly compared to similar tools from SiteGround, Hostinger and Ionos . The first issue was that domain registration required a phone number — something I haven’t encountered with other web hosts. Hosting.com didn’t immediately recognize my number, so I had to contact customer service to figure out the required format and complete registration. Hosting.com support told me the domain would automatically point to the correct servers once it finished registering, but the processing didn’t work correctly, forcing me to contact customer support again. Once my domain was pointed at the correct servers, Hosting.com gave me options to quickly migrate a site or build one of my own. WordPress installation was fast and included a choice to preinstall WooCommerce, but provided none of the guidance on themes or plugins offered by companies like SiteGround. There was also no onboarding plugin, something included with WordPress hosting from most competitors. Hosting.com directed me to the regular WordPress dashboard instead, which is fine for me but may overwhelm new users. To top it all off, WordPress immediately told me that my site’s PHP was out of date. Every other web host I’ve tested in 2026 installed my WordPress site using the latest PHP, so this was a surprise. Hosting.com’s managed WordPress tools make it easy to update PHP without entering the often-overwhelming cPanel, but this may be more difficult if you’re on shared hosting. Server management is frustrating at first, as common tasks are kept in disparate and often confusing areas. The Domains area, for example, doesn’t include options for editing DNS records; you edit those in the Products and Services section . The proprietary DNS editor is beginner-friendly, but finding it is more challenging than it needs to be. Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET If you’re using shared hosting, you can access server management in the expected place — Hosting & Servers. But WordPress hosting users must go to the Managed WordPress area. While the tools are beginner-friendly for basic server-related tasks, I wish they were easier to find. Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET Advanced tasks like database management are conducted through the industry-standard cPanel. While cPanel can be complicated for new users, developers should enjoy using the familiar tool. Hosting.com’s use of cPanel for back-end tasks may also make it easier to switch web hosts later on, as some web hosts’ free migration services rely on cPanel. Performance: Where Hosting.com shines Key takeaway: Hosting.com uses fast, reliable servers to ensure visitors can always access your website quickly. Server performance determines how quickly and reliably visitors can access your website. I tracked uptime and site speed for my Hosting.com test site over one week: Uptime: The percentage of time your website spends online. The best web hosts offer uptime guarantees of at least 99.9%, as folks who find your website down may go elsewhere, resulting in lost traffic and potentially revenue. Site speed: The number of seconds your site takes to load. Experts recommend aiming for a loading time of less than two seconds, as conversion rates drop by 1% to 3% for every 100 milliseconds beyond the two-second mark. My Hosting.com site performed remarkably well, with a 100% uptime only matched by SiteGround and a 2.55-second site speed that outstrips default speeds of every host I’ve tested so far. Uptime was excellent Hosting.com offers the industry-standard 99.9% uptime guarantee on its shared hosting plans, so server issues shouldn’t cause more than 10 minutes of downtime per week. WordPress plans, meanwhile, offer an above-average 99.99% uptime guarantee, meaning server issues shouldn’t cause more than two minutes of downtime per week. I monitored my site’s uptime (using a WordPress hosting plan) for one week with BetterStack , and my site had no downtime that week, suggesting that Hosting.com lives up to its guarantees. Site speed outstripped other hosts’ default speeds I simulated loading my site in various locations with WebPageTest , resulting in the following average speeds (times are in seconds): Location US UK Germany India Dubai Australia Overall Desktop 1.55 1.44 1.69 2.27 1.65 1.95 1.75 Mobile 3 2.9 3.28 3.49 3.62 3.92 3.36 Combined, I clocked desktop and mobile averages of 2.55 seconds, faster than top competitors like SiteGround and Hostinger. Hostinger pulled ahead with a site speed of 2.46 seconds after enabling caching and a CDN, but these results show that Hosting.com is still one of the fastest web hosts on the market. Nevertheless, 2.55 seconds is over the recommended two-second maximum, so I recommend taking additional steps to improve your site speed . Performance tools are great and automatically enabled Hosting.com uses LiteSpeed-enhanced servers with built-in caching, a protocol that stores website data in fast-access layers to reduce the resources required to load a website. Since this is the default server build, you don’t need to enable or configure caching settings to enjoy improved site speed. WordPress hosting plans use an enterprise-level CDN or content delivery network, storing data in a series of interconnected web servers around the globe. This reduces loading times by letting users’ devices retrieve data from a server close to their location rather than pulling from a data center on the other side of the world. Because the CDN is automatically enabled, you don’t need to do anything to reap the benefits. Shared hosting users don’t get automated CDN access, but Hosting.com makes it easy to connect your site to a third-party CDN like Cloudflare. Security: Robust protection from the most common threats Key takeaway: Hosting.com includes basic security protocols and tools needed to protect your data and website from various common threats. Additionally, its automated daily backups — something other hosts often restrict to specific plans — are included on even the lowest-cost plan. Every Hosting.com plan includes features to keep your data safe, prevent your site from being overwhelmed and simplify rebooting your site if something goes wrong: SSL certification : A protocol that encrypts data sent to and from your site, like information submitted through a contact form, so it’s difficult for malicious users to intercept. Google, browsers and VPNs consider SSL certification a key safety indicator, making it essential if you want people to find and use your site. Firewall : Software that scans incoming and outgoing traffic for signs of malicious intent, blocking anything it deems suspicious. Firewalls can’t guarantee 100% protection, but a good one can identify and block most threats. DDoS protection : Protocols for identifying and blocking distributed denial-of-service attacks, which flood your website with malicious traffic intended to shut down your server. Automated daily backups: Backups of your entire website completed every day, with an easy restore option to help you get up and running again if something shuts your site down. Hosting.com’s included features protect you from the most common security threats. There’s no malware scanner, but many companies — even SiteGround, one of the most secure web hosts in the industry — don’t offer built-in malware scanners. Assuming regular firewall updates, you shouldn’t need one, as the firewall will protect your site from malware. Customer service: The biggest disappointment Key takeaway: Hosting.com’s customer service responds quickly, but isn’t always helpful. I explored Hosting.com’s knowledge base and tested its live chat and email support to determine its speed and helpfulness in troubleshooting various issues. Many knowledge base articles lacked images, making them unhelpful for visual learners. Additionally, while I consistently received prompt responses from Hosting.com support, the first agent I spoke to rarely resolved my issues, resulting in long, frustrating interactions. I recommend SiteGround or Ionos if you expect to need customer support regularly. Knowledge base and tutorials are lacking Screenshot by Dianna Gunn/CNET Hosting.com’s knowledge base looks good at first glance, with a prominent search bar, sidebar of handy links and buttons for categories of commonly asked questions. Unfortunately, some links return 404 errors, and several tutorials are walls of text without any images. I also didn’t find a single video in the articles I read, making Hosting.com a particularly poor choice for visual learners. I recommend Hostinger or SiteGround if you want solid self-serve support options. Direct communication was frustrating Hosting.com’s live chat and email support offer fast response times, but the quality of support is severely lacking. Asking anything beyond the most basic questions resulted in being passed between multiple support representatives before I found someone able to resolve my problems, suggesting that Hosting.com’s training for support representatives is inconsistent. The chatbot answered my simplest questions immediately, with step-by-step processes for fixing them. When I encountered a DNS error, it directed me to a human agent who responded within two minutes. However, the agent’s answer — to wait for the DNS to finish propagating — was incorrect, forcing me to contact support again the following day. The second agent I spoke to fixed my DNS problem within a few minutes, but having to reach out twice to resolve a common error leaves me doubting support’s ability to fix more complex problems. Next, I submitted a support ticket. The bot responded immediately, but its explanation was incorrect. It passed me to human support, which informed me that my query had been sent to a specialist team. The specialist responded an hour later — unusually fast for email support — saying they didn’t understand my issue, despite reading my conversation with the support bot. I sent further clarification and was transferred to a third person, who finally fixed my problem. The whole interaction took about two hours and was deeply frustrating. Reputation is excellent Hosting.com has a 4.8 out of 5-star Trustpilot rating . To my surprise, most positive reviews cited a more pleasant customer service experience than my own. This suggests that my problems with support may be unusual. However, I still find it difficult to recommend Hosting.com’s customer service based on my experience. Hosting.com provides fast, reliable servers and decent value, but it’s only suitable for power users Hosting.com has some of the fastest, most reliable servers around, plus solid prices for shared and WordPress hosting that can make it a powerful choice for small websites like personal blogs or professional portfolios. However, its unintuitive setup processes and frustrating customer support make it a poor choice for beginners. If you’re looking for a simpler website creation process, I recommend Ionos for personal websites and SiteGround for business websites. Dianna Gunn Web Hosting Expert Dianna Gunn built her first WordPress website in 2008. Since then, she's poured thousands of hours into understanding how websites and online businesses work. She's shared what she's learned on blogs like ThemeIsle, BloggingPro and DomainWheel. She now works for CNET as a Web Hosting Expert, creating in-depth guides on web hosting and reviewing the top web hosting companies to help folks preparing to build a website for the first time. text: X A2 Hosting (Now Hosting.com) Review for 2026 (Tested) Last updated on February 11th, 2026 by Alvin Collin Facebook Tweet LinkedIn Pin Shares 0 I’ve built more WordPress sites than I can count. The reality is that there are so many hosting companies out there. It’s overwhelming! Every hosting company claims to be the fastest, the most reliable. But you never really know how a host performs until you try it yourself. So I did just that. Their team is available 24/7 and helped me fix a plugin issue without pushing upsells or wasting time. Something I appreciated. On top of that, they were kind, patient, and knew exactly what to do. They also migrated one of my existing sites for free . I didn’t have to lift a finger. It was one less thing to stress about. Hosting.com Hosting Key Features: High-performance turbo servers Free SSD Two great operating system options Anytime money-back guarantee Get started with Hosting.com today! Hosting Types Features Performance Customer Support Ease of Use Pricing FAQs Final Verdict With that said, let us get into it. Again, I was pleasantly surprised that the unmanaged VPS service also comes provisioned with the Linux OS if you want to use it. That way, you only need to pay for the specific resources you’ll need. Managed VPS plans, on the other hand, allow you to use either Windows or Linux OS. All Linux hosting plans come with cPanel control panel for managing your hosting account. VPS Hosting Key Features: Both managed and unmanaged options Perpetual security Configure VPS the way you want Choose your data center location Get started with Hosting.com today! Hosting.com WordPress Hosting Since WordPress powers IsItWP and many of my other sites, I paid extra attention when testing Hosting.com’s WordPress plans . Here’s what I found: if you’re after a fast, reliable WordPress host that doesn’t break the bank, Hosting.com is the perfect fit for you. They stand out by offering both shared WordPress hosting and managed WordPress hosting . For those just starting, shared WordPress hosting is a great budget-friendly option. But if you’re after more power and a few extra features, like creating a staging site with a single click, a free Jetpack personal license, automatic backups , and WP-CLI pre-installed, managed WordPress hosting is the way to go. With both plans, Hosting.com sets up WordPress for you right out of the box. They also include Let’s Encrypt SSL, which means your site gets extra protection without any hassle. All plans come with a WHM control panel and a free eNom reseller account. With an eNom reseller account, you can resell domain names to your customers . With a Silver level or higher plan, you get free WHMCS that enable you to manage every aspect of your customers’ hosting accounts. Your reseller account is fully white labeled so your customers will never know that they’re actually being hosted on Hosting.com. Besides a custom control panel, you can also offer free custom nameservers which further allow you to rebrand your hosting services. Hosting.com Reseller Hosting Key Features: WHM control panel Free eNnom reseller account Optional WHMCS access Both Windows and Linux hosting available Get started with Hosting.com today! Hosting.com cPanel Hosting Plans With powerful cPanel hosting , you get a user-friendly control panel that simplifies server management, complete with a handy file manager to keep your web files in check. Setting up is as easy as it gets with 1-Click cPanel Installation via Softaculous. This is an old but reliable tool that lets you install popular apps like WordPress, Drupal, or Joomla with a single click. You’ll be live in minutes, no complicated setup needed. Hosting.com delivers reliable and easy-to-use site management. Whether you’re new to hosting or a seasoned pro, cPanel’s intuitive design makes running your site smooth and stress-free. The base plan comes with 15GB of disk space, allowing ample room for your website’s files and growth. Plus, you get 1 MariaDB included. This fast, open-source database system stores and manages your site’s data , like blog posts or user info, perfect for powering platforms like WordPress. Since this is a business hosting plan, the easy Google Workspace setup l ets you integrate email , calendars , and more from your hosting dashboard. It’s a game-changer for small businesses or anyone wanting a polished online presence. For WordPress users, the WP Toolkit is a dream come true. It simplifies editing and updating your plugins, themes, and settings—no coding required. Keep your site fresh and functional with minimal effort. Worried about losing your work? With automatic cPanel backups , your data is regularly saved. If anything goes wrong, you can restore your site with a few clicks—peace of mind included. Plus, the MultiPHP Manager lets you change your site’s PHP version easily, ensuring compatibility with whatever apps you’re running. It’s like giving your site a custom upgrade. Want insights into your site’s performance? Awstats has you covered. This analytics tool tracks user behavior and website traffic , helping you understand what’s working and where to improve. Hosting.com Cpanel Hosting Key Features cPanel is your one-stop shop for website tasks. From a single, centralized interface, you can: Manage domains Organize web files Configure email settings Oversee software installations That is it for the Hosting.com Hosting types. Let us look at features next. Features As with all my hosting reviews, I focus on features as a key area. I look for unique features that can give me and my clients an advantage. I like that Hosting.com stands out with its Turbo servers for faster performance, free site migrations , and automatic backups . On top of that, our more experienced WordPress experts enjoyed the developer-friendly tools like SSH access and staging environments.
